title: The Blind Spot in the Dressing Room
notes: Detective-cast (Conan, Masumi Sera, Sonoko, Ran, Inspector Megure) omitted by convention. No `event` node type: actions are direct typed edges. The old cases/ file correctly identified Yamaki as the culprit and the debt/humiliation motive, but it collapsed the entire mechanism into a single generic murder event and left out: the dying-message decoding (victim's own nails + Chinese finger-counting spelling 'Ya' for Yamaki), the fabricated decoy sandals (built on the spot from a shoe insole, ribbon, tape and a phone to fake a fourth customer's presence and free up the middle changing room), the chloroform-soaked face-cover trick used to silently knock the victim out before strangling her, and a first, botched attempt the prior week where the same chloroform trap knocked out the wrong woman (Nitsuka) instead of the intended victim. The old file's summary of the humiliation ('dressing her pet dog in the same outfit as her assistant') also has the direction backwards: per the transcript, the president had Yamaki's own clothes remade into dog clothes and put a collar/leash on Yamaki herself, i.e. she dressed the *employee* to match the dog, not the other way around. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: Victim's right thumb, reddened with her own lipstick around her five-star nail art, forms the Chinese flag; her left-hand shape, otherwise misreadable as a European number or a gun, matches the Chinese one-hand count for 'eight' -- the first sound of 'Yamaki'.

Nitsuka, Nanbu, and Yamaki independently sketch the same distinctive white sandals supposedly left by a fourth customer, but store security footage never shows anyone wearing them leaving -- the sandals never existed as a real customer's shoes.
